referencesZh.use: 支持固定源近似下E=F/q与F=qE，以及正负试探电荷的受力方向和向量关系。

referencesZh.citation: OpenStax. University Physics Volume 2, §5.6 Electric Field Lines.
referencesZh.use: 支持场线作为电场的绘图表示而非物质线或粒子轨迹；静态图本身不测传播速度。

articles.title: Three Test Spheres Send Gu Yan to Check the Batch Labels First
articles.summary: The reference record for point P in the electrostatic deflection device is about 200 N/C to the right. Gu Yan keeps the source setting and point P fixed and obtains independent force measurements using three small known charges. All three F/q values are about +200 N/C, so she checks probe batches first rather than interpreting the force changes directly as changes in the background quantity at P.
storyParagraphs: After three new batches of test spheres are introduced on the packaging line’s electrostatic deflection device, force readings at the same marked point P are no longer the same. Maintenance technician Gu Yan has a reference from the previous calibration: the external electric field at P was about 200 N/C to the right. Rather than dismantling the source electrode first, she locks the current source setting and the position of P and retests with three spheres of known charge.

F on the work order denotes the external electric force on a sphere, with rightward force positive and leftward force negative; 1 μC=10⁻⁶ C. For the first sphere, q=+1 μC and the measured force is F=+0.0002 N; calculating E=F/q gives +200 N/C. For the second sphere, q=+2 μC and F=+0.0004 N, again giving E=+200 N/C. The force is larger, but it increases in proportion with the charge.

For the third sphere, q=−1 μC and the measured force reverses to the left, F=−0.0002 N. A negative force divided by a negative charge still gives E=+200 N/C, directed to the right. Gu Yan writes all three E results beside the reference value: they agree with the earlier value of about 200 N/C at P, so there is at least no sign that merely changing the probe requires reversing the field arrow at P.

Gu Yan adds each sphere’s q beside its force reading and opens a column for F/q. All three rows say +200 N/C. She places the old calibration record beside that column. The force arrows have different lengths and directions, yet dividing by their respective charges returns the same reference value at P. She closes the tool case laid out for dismantling the source and picks up the three batch labels first. At this stage of today’s check, she does not yet need to move the electrode.

She also notes the small-test-charge approximation on the work order. The probe itself also produces an electric field, but here it is assumed small enough that its disturbance of the source distribution is negligible. In F=qE, E refers to the external field produced by the source; the probe’s own field is not counted as a same-type self-force pushing the probe itself.

In the afternoon, Gu Yan returns the three spheres to their labeled boxes, while the wrench stays on the tool cart. Beside the tape mark at P, the reference arrow remains pointed right at about 200 N/C. Under it are the three force records: +0.0002, +0.0004, and −0.0002 N. She goes first to verify the labels and certificates for the three new sphere batches, then decides whether the source electrode needs further disassembly.
articles.overall: A field concept assigns a physical quantity to each point in space and time. This article uses the electric-field vector to separate the external field established by the source at P from the force response of a test charge. With source and position fixed, F=qE changes with q while E can remain consistent.
explanationParagraphs: A field concept assigns a physical quantity to points in space/time; the electric field is a vector and can be defined through the external force per unit small positive test charge. Here, all three F/q values are about 200 N/C to the right.

Right is positive and left is negative, with μC=10⁻⁶ C. The probe must be small enough to avoid appreciably disturbing the source. Agreement across the three readings supports only the current static check at P and does not prove that the whole device has no other fault.

module.intro: Infer the external field at P from independent force measurements and compare it with a reference, rather than generating forces from an assumed field and then using them to verify that same assumption.
module.diagramTitle: How Three q Values and Three F Values All Return to About +200 N/C
diagramSteps: Fix the source setting and point P, and read the historical reference field of about +200 N/C
Use +1 μC and +0.0002 N to infer E
Use +2 μC and +0.0004 N to infer E
Use −1 μC and −0.0002 N to infer E
After all three agree, check probe batches first rather than immediately dismantling the source
diagramStepNotes: Sign convention: right is positive and left is negative; 1 μC=10⁻⁶ C.
When charge doubles, force doubles.
A negative probe feels force in the opposite direction, but F/q still gives the same rightward external field.
The conclusion is limited to the current static check at fixed point P.
mapping: Tape mark at P → fixed spatial position.
Historical reference arrow → a comparison baseline independent of the current three force measurements.
Three spheres with known q → changing probe properties.
Wrench left on the tool cart → limited evidence changes the troubleshooting order rather than declaring the source absolutely normal.
module.boundary: The force and reference values are fictional electrostatic records. Spheres are approximated as point charges, and F is external electric force. F=qE describes electric force; the small-probe condition makes source disturbance negligible so the approximately unperturbed source field can be read. A probe that appreciably rearranges source charges may change the background E. This example neither measures propagation speed nor excludes faults elsewhere or of other kinds.
module.reflection: Why can three spheres experience different force magnitudes and directions while still being consistent with the same external electric field at point P?

references.citation: OpenStax. University Physics Volume 2, §5.4 Electric Field.
references.use: Supports E=F/q and F=qE under the fixed-source approximation, including the force direction and vector relationship for positive and negative test charges.

references.citation: OpenStax. University Physics Volume 2, §5.6 Electric Field Lines.
references.use: Supports field lines as a graphical representation of the electric field rather than material lines or particle trajectories; a static diagram by itself does not measure propagation speed.

articles.titleZh: 按多少步也到不了(2,2)，三个按钮哪里限制了路线
articles.summaryZh: 关卡从(1,2)出发，只允许左边+2、右边+2或交换两项。测试失败本身不是证明；乔宁改为对任意状态(x,y)逐一检查三种合法操作，得到能覆盖任意有限按钮序列的奇偶限制。
storyParagraphsZh: 乔宁在调一个双计数器关卡。状态是非负整数对(x,y)，初态(1,2)，按钮只有“左+2”“右+2”“交换”。她把(2,2)设成目标，因为看起来只差一点；测试员试过几条路线都到不了，但这还可能只是没搜够。
她不再记录某几次具体按键，而是从任意状态(x,y)写三条合法规则：(x,y)→(x+2,y)、(x,y)→(x,y+2)、(x,y)→(y,x)。前两种让总和x+y恰好增加2，交换让总和保持不变，因此三种情况都保持(x+y)的奇偶性。
初态(1,2)的总和是3，为奇数。第0步先满足这一性质；若某一步后的状态总和是奇数，那么下一次无论按哪一个合法按钮，奇偶仍保持。因此按归纳思路，任何有限长度的合法按钮序列到达的状态，总和都仍是奇数，而不是只在已经试过的路线中如此。
(2,2)的总和是4，为偶数，所以被直接排除。乔宁再看候选(0,1)：它的总和1同样是奇数，因此不被奇偶条件排除；但三个按钮中，两个加法只增总和，交换不改总和，总和从初态3永远不会降到1，所以它仍不可达。
她最后选了一个确实能到的目标(2,3)。这次不是因为它总和为5就宣布可达，而是实际找到路线：(1,2)先按左+2到(3,2)，再交换到(2,3)。相同奇偶只去掉一道障碍，真正的可达仍需额外条件或具体路线。乔宁把这条路线保存成关卡的自动测试。
关卡保存时，目标框已经从(2,2)换成(2,3)，三个按钮仍原样保留。记录旁边同时放着两个标签：“(2,2)：奇偶冲突”“(0,1)：奇偶相同但总和降不下去”。她重新运行自动测试，两步后目标框亮起，两个不可达示例仍留在说明区。
articles.overallZh: 不变量方法先固定状态集和全部合法操作，再证明某个量或关系被每一步保持。由初态和逐步保持性可推广到任意有限合法序列；目标若取不同值即可排除可达，取相同值则只表示没有被这一条件排除。
explanationParagraphsZh: 对任意(x,y)，三种规则使x+y分别变为x+y+2、x+y+2、x+y，因此I=(x+y) mod2每一步保持。初态I=1，所以(2,2)的I=0不可达。
(0,1)也有I=1却仍不可达，因为总和不能下降；而(2,3)有具体两步路线。相同I不是可达性的充分条件。

moduleZh.intro: 把三种按钮写成对任意(x,y)都成立的规则，再用初态与逐步保持性覆盖任意有限序列。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从任意一步保持奇偶到排除(2,2)
diagramSteps: 固定非负整数状态集和全部三个合法操作
对任意(x,y)证明三种操作都保持总和奇偶
用初态I=1和逐步保持性推广到任意有限序列
以(2,2)和(0,1)分别展示不同I与相同I的后果
用具体两步路线确认(2,3)确实可达
diagramStepNotes: 按钮只有左+2、右+2、交换，没有−2、+1、重置或自由改值。
总和变化分别为+2、+2、0，所以I=(x+y) mod2均不变。
初态(1,2)在第0步有I=1；若某一步I=1，三条规则使下一步仍有I=1，所以每个有限步数都保持这一性质。
(2,2)因I=0被排除；(0,1)虽I=1，但受总和不减限制仍不可达。
(1,2)→(3,2)→(2,3)给出实际可达路线并被保存为自动测试。
mapping: 三个按钮 → 证明必须覆盖的全部合法操作。
目标(2,2) → 因不变量值不同被整体排除。
候选(0,1) → 相同不变量值仍不保证可达。
保存后的目标(2,3) → 由具体合法路线确认的可达状态。
moduleZh.boundary: 不变量依赖当前状态集和全部允许操作。不同不变量值足以排除可达，相同值并不充分。若按钮集合改变，必须重新检查保持性；但增加某个新按钮并不自动意味着当前奇偶一定被破坏。这里的证明针对任意有限合法序列。
moduleZh.reflection: 另开两份规则副本，分别新增“左+1”与“左+4”，原三按钮仍保留。先算新操作使x+y改变多少：哪份仍可沿用原奇偶证明，哪份必须停止沿用？即使奇偶保持，为什么(0,1)仍提醒你不能仅凭相同I宣布可达？

referencesZh.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, 5.4.3 The Invariant Principle. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
referencesZh.use: 支持由初态性质和所有合法变换的保持性推出所有可达状态满足该性质，并用性质不同排除目标可达性。

referencesZh.citation: James Aspnes. IOAutomata, 2.2.1 Safety properties. Yale University online course notes (undated).
referencesZh.use: 支持通过归纳说明性质在所有可达状态保持；该性质不必是可达状态集合的完整刻画。

articles.title: Why Can No Number of Legal Moves Reach (2,2)?
articles.summary: The level starts at (1,2) and permits only “left +2,” “right +2,” or swapping the two entries. Failed testing is not a proof. Qiao Ning instead checks all three legal operations for an arbitrary state (x,y), obtaining a parity restriction that covers every finite button sequence.
storyParagraphs: Qiao Ning is tuning a two-counter level. A state is a pair of nonnegative integers (x,y), the starting state is (1,2), and the only buttons are “left +2,” “right +2,” and “swap.” She sets (2,2) as the target because it looks close. The tester tries several routes and never reaches it, but that could still mean the search is incomplete.

Instead of recording a few specific button presses, she writes all three legal rules from an arbitrary state (x,y): (x,y)→(x+2,y), (x,y)→(x,y+2), and (x,y)→(y,x). The first two increase x+y by exactly 2, while the swap leaves the sum unchanged. Therefore all three preserve the parity of x+y.

The starting state (1,2) has sum 3, which is odd. The property holds at step 0. If the sum is odd after any step, then no matter which legal button is pressed next, parity remains unchanged. By this inductive reasoning, every state reached by any finite legal button sequence still has an odd sum, not merely the states on routes already tested.

The target (2,2) has sum 4, which is even, so it is excluded immediately. Qiao Ning then checks candidate (0,1): its sum 1 is also odd, so parity does not exclude it. But among the three buttons, the two additions only increase the sum and the swap leaves it unchanged. The sum can never fall from the starting value 3 to 1, so (0,1) is still unreachable.

She finally chooses a target that really is reachable: (2,3). This time she does not declare success merely because its sum 5 is odd. She finds an actual route: from (1,2), press left +2 to get (3,2), then swap to get (2,3). Matching parity removes only one obstacle; actual reachability still needs other conditions or a concrete route. Qiao Ning saves this route as an automated test for the level.

When the level is saved, the target box has changed from (2,2) to (2,3), while the three buttons remain unchanged. Two labels sit beside the record: “(2,2): parity conflict” and “(0,1): matching parity, but sum cannot decrease.” She reruns the automated test; after two steps, the target box lights up, while both unreachable examples remain in the explanation panel.
articles.overall: Invariance methods begin by fixing the state space and all legal operations, then proving that a quantity or relation is preserved at every step. The initial state plus stepwise preservation extends to every finite legal sequence. A target with a different invariant value can be ruled out; a target with the same value is merely not excluded by that condition.
explanationParagraphs: For arbitrary (x,y), the three rules change x+y to x+y+2, x+y+2, and x+y, so I=(x+y) mod 2 is preserved at every step. The initial state has I=1, so target (2,2) with I=0 is unreachable.
(0,1) also has I=1 but is still unreachable because the sum cannot decrease, while (2,3) has a concrete two-step route. Matching I is not sufficient for reachability.

module.intro: Write the three buttons as rules valid for arbitrary (x,y), then use the initial state and stepwise preservation to cover every finite sequence.
module.diagramTitle: From Parity Preservation at Every Step to Excluding (2,2)
diagramSteps: Fix the nonnegative-integer state space and all three legal operations
Prove for arbitrary (x,y) that every operation preserves sum parity
Use initial I=1 and stepwise preservation to extend to every finite legal sequence
Use (2,2) and (0,1) to show the consequences of different and matching I values
Confirm that (2,3) is actually reachable with a concrete two-step route
diagramStepNotes: The only buttons are left +2, right +2, and swap; there is no −2, +1, reset, or free reassignment.
The sum changes by +2, +2, and 0, so I=(x+y) mod 2 is unchanged in all cases.
The start (1,2) has I=1 at step 0. If I=1 at any step, all three rules keep I=1 at the next step, so the property holds after every finite number of moves.
(2,2) is excluded because I=0; (0,1) has I=1 but remains unreachable because the sum cannot decrease.
(1,2)→(3,2)→(2,3) is a real reachable route and is saved as an automated test.
mapping: Three buttons → the complete set of legal operations the proof must cover.
Target (2,2) → a state excluded because its invariant value differs.
Candidate (0,1) → a state showing that matching the invariant still does not guarantee reachability.
Saved target (2,3) → a reachable state confirmed by a concrete legal route.
module.boundary: The invariant depends on the current state space and the full set of allowed operations. Different invariant values are sufficient to rule out reachability; matching values are not sufficient. If the button set changes, preservation must be checked again, but adding a new button does not automatically mean the current parity property is broken. This proof concerns arbitrary finite legal sequences.
module.reflection: Make two separate copies of the rules, adding “left +1” to one and “left +4” to the other while keeping the original three buttons. Calculate each new operation’s change to x+y. Which copy can retain the parity proof, and which cannot? Even when parity is preserved, why does (0,1) still warn against declaring reachability from matching I alone?

references.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, 5.4.3 The Invariant Principle. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
references.use: Supports using a property of the initial state together with preservation under every legal transformation to show that all reachable states retain the property, and using a different property value to rule out a target.

references.citation: James Aspnes. IOAutomata, 2.2.1 Safety properties. Yale University online course notes (undated).
references.use: Supports proving by induction that a property holds in all reachable states; such a property need not provide a complete characterization of the reachable-state set.

articles.titleZh: 数轴上能不能放一个“最小正刻度”
articles.summaryZh: 陆弦要判断全部正有理数中是否存在最小元素。候选1/10、1/20、1/40不断向0靠近，却不能处理全体；她转而准确假设“存在一个最小正有理数r”，再从同一论域构造r/2。
storyParagraphsZh: 陆弦在做一条抽象有理数数轴。界面需要一个开关：“显示最小正刻度”。同事先把标记放在1/10，很快有人指出1/20更小；再试1/40也一样。候选不断向0靠近，却始终找不到一个可以保证停下的位置。更多候选只会继续搜索，不会自动变成一般证明。
她先固定论域Q+={a/b:a,b为正整数}，采用通常大小关系，不限制分母、显示精度或格点数量。要判断的命题是“Q+没有最小元素”；它的准确否定是：存在r∈Q+，使得对所有s∈Q+都有r≤s。陆弦暂时接受这个否定，准备只用它和有理数定义继续推。
因为r∈Q+，可以写成r=a/b，其中a、b都是正整数。她构造s=a/(2b)=r/2。由于b是正整数，2b仍是正整数，a也仍为正整数，所以s仍属于同一个Q+；这一步没有换论域，也没有预先使用“没有最小元素”这一目标结论。
接下来比较大小：r>0，所以s=r/2>0，并且s<r。于是同一个Q+里出现了一个合法s，却比假定的最小元素r更小；这直接冲突于“对所有s∈Q+都有r≤s”。冲突来自最小性假设和已接受定义，因此该存在假设不能保留。所以Q+没有最小元素；这里撤销的是“存在最小者”的假设，不只是排除某个具体候选。
陆弦再切到独立对照集合T={n/100:n为正整数}。对任意n≥1，都有n/100≥1/100，所以1/100确实是T的最小元素；1/200不属于T，因为它不能写成正整数n除以100。原来的r/2构造在这个论域里不保证仍是合法对象。
页面保存时，Q+模式下“最小正刻度”开关保持关闭；T模式下则显示1/100。旁边仍留着1/10、1/20、1/40三个旧候选，只作为有限搜索为何不足的记录。数轴上的0仍标成边界点，没有被写成正有理数，也没有暗示不断减半能在有限步到达0。
articles.overallZh: 反证法先准确写出目标命题的否定，暂时接受它，并只使用该假设与已接受前提进行有效推理。若由此得到真正的逻辑冲突，就撤销该假设。矛盾不能来自偷换论域、错误代数、测量误差或循环使用目标结论。
explanationParagraphsZh: 假设存在最小正有理数r=a/b，则a,b为正整数，s=a/(2b)=r/2仍属于Q+，且0<s<r，与“对所有s都有r≤s”直接冲突。
在T={n/100:n为正整数}中，n≥1推出n/100≥1/100，所以1/100确为最小；1/200不属于T。论域一变，原构造可能不再合法。

moduleZh.intro: 先写命题与准确否定，再检查构造对象始终留在同一论域，并确认矛盾确实依赖所作假设。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 假设最小r存在，为什么r/2会直接冲突
diagramSteps: 固定Q+并写出“没有最小元素”的准确否定
暂时假设存在r∈Q+且对所有s都有r≤s
写r=a/b并构造s=a/(2b)
验证s∈Q+且0<s<r形成直接矛盾
用T={n/100:n为正整数}检查新论域为何可以有最小元素
diagramStepNotes: Q+由a,b为正整数的a/b组成；0不属于Q+。
假设内容必须包括r∈Q+以及对所有合法s的最小性条件。
a,b为正整数，所以2b仍为正整数，s=a/(2b)仍合法。
r>0推出0<r/2<r，与“对所有s有r≤s”冲突。
T限定n为正整数，所以n≥1且n/100≥1/100；1/100在T中最小，1/200对应n=1/2而不属于T。
mapping: 向0靠近的1/10、1/20、1/40 → 有限候选搜索无法证明全体命题。
假定的r=a/b → 从任意最小候选出发，而非特例。
s=r/2 → 在同一Q+内构造的冲突对象。
T={n/100:n为正整数} → 指定新论域后最小元素存在的独立对照。
moduleZh.boundary: 0是Q+的下确界但不属于Q+，因此不是最小正有理数；不断减半也不表示有限步到达0。固定分母、有限精度或其他离散集合可能有最小元素。反证中的冲突必须来自目标假设和一致前提，而非错误代数、循环论证或换论域。
moduleZh.reflection: 有人也把T={n/100:n为正整数}中的1/100减半，得到更小的1/200。为什么这不能推翻T的最小值？请指出与Q+的r/2推导相比，哪一项对象合法性检查没有通过。

referencesZh.citation: Richard Hammack. Book of Proof, 3rd edition (edition 3.4), 6.1 Proving Statements with Contradiction. Richard Hammack (2018; revised 2025).
referencesZh.use: 支持假定目标命题的否定、经有效推理得到与该假定冲突，再撤销假定的证明结构；本篇例子不是历史发现叙事。

referencesZh.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, 1.8 Proof by Contradiction. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
referencesZh.use: 支持反证结构及对推理有效性的检查；正有理数最小值算例由有理数定义和次序关系独立演算，不归为教材中的历史案例。

articles.title: Can a Number Line Display a “Smallest Positive Tick”?
articles.summary: Lu Xian needs to decide whether the positive rational numbers contain a smallest element. Candidates 1/10, 1/20, and 1/40 move closer and closer to 0 but cannot settle the entire set. She instead assumes precisely that a smallest positive rational r exists and constructs r/2 within the same domain.
storyParagraphs: Lu Xian is building an abstract rational-number line. The interface needs a switch labeled “show smallest positive tick.” A colleague first places the marker at 1/10, and someone quickly points out that 1/20 is smaller; 1/40 fails in the same way. The candidates keep moving toward 0, but there is never a point where she can guarantee that the search should stop. More candidates only continue the search; they do not automatically become a general proof.

She first fixes the domain Q+={a/b : a,b are positive integers}, with the usual ordering and no restriction on denominators, display precision, or grid size. The claim to decide is “Q+ has no smallest element.” Its exact negation is: there exists r∈Q+ such that for every s∈Q+, r≤s. Lu Xian temporarily accepts this negation and proceeds using only it and the definition of rational numbers.

Because r∈Q+, it can be written as r=a/b, where a and b are positive integers. She constructs s=a/(2b)=r/2. Since b is a positive integer, 2b is also a positive integer, and a remains positive, so s still belongs to the same Q+. This step does not change domains and does not assume in advance the target conclusion that there is no smallest element.

Now she compares sizes. Since r>0, s=r/2>0, and s<r. Thus the same Q+ contains a valid s that is smaller than the supposedly smallest element r. This directly conflicts with “for every s∈Q+, r≤s.” The conflict follows from the minimality assumption together with the accepted definition, so the existence assumption cannot be retained. Therefore Q+ has no smallest element: what has been rejected is the existence of a minimum, not merely one specific candidate.

Lu Xian then switches to an independent comparison set T={n/100 : n is a positive integer}. For every n≥1, n/100≥1/100, so 1/100 really is the smallest element of T. The number 1/200 is not in T because it cannot be written as a positive integer n divided by 100. The earlier r/2 construction is not guaranteed to stay legal in this new domain.

When the page is saved, the “smallest positive tick” switch remains off in Q+ mode, while T mode displays 1/100. The old candidates 1/10, 1/20, and 1/40 remain beside the line only as a record of why finite search is insufficient. The point 0 remains marked as a boundary point, not as a positive rational, and repeated halving is not presented as reaching 0 in finitely many steps.
articles.overall: Proof by contradiction begins by writing the exact negation of the target claim, temporarily accepting it, and reasoning only from that assumption together with accepted premises. If valid reasoning produces a genuine logical conflict, the assumption is rejected. The conflict must not come from changing domains, algebraic error, measurement error, or circular use of the desired conclusion.
explanationParagraphs: Assume that a smallest positive rational r=a/b exists, where a and b are positive integers. Then s=a/(2b)=r/2 is still in Q+ and satisfies 0<s<r, directly contradicting “r≤s for every s.”
In T={n/100 : n is a positive integer}, n≥1 implies n/100≥1/100, so 1/100 really is the minimum, while 1/200 is not in T. Changing the domain can make the earlier construction invalid.

module.intro: Write the claim and its exact negation first, then check that every constructed object remains in the same domain and that the contradiction genuinely depends on the assumption.
module.diagramTitle: Assume a Smallest r Exists—Why Does r/2 Create a Direct Conflict?
diagramSteps: Fix Q+ and write the exact negation of “there is no smallest element”
Temporarily assume r∈Q+ and r≤s for every s∈Q+
Write r=a/b and construct s=a/(2b)
Verify s∈Q+ and 0<s<r, producing a direct contradiction
Use T={n/100 : n is a positive integer} to check why the new domain can have a minimum
diagramStepNotes: Q+ consists of a/b with a and b positive integers; 0 is not in Q+.
The assumption must include both r∈Q+ and its minimality relative to every legal s.
Because a and b are positive integers, 2b is a positive integer and s=a/(2b) remains legal.
r>0 implies 0<r/2<r, contradicting “r≤s for every s.”
T restricts n to positive integers, so n≥1 and n/100≥1/100. Its minimum is 1/100; 1/200 would require n=1/2 and is not in T.
mapping: 1/10, 1/20, 1/40 moving toward 0 → finite candidate search cannot prove the universal claim.
Assumed r=a/b → an arbitrary supposed minimum rather than a special case.
s=r/2 → a conflicting object constructed within the same Q+.
T={n/100 : n is a positive integer} → an independent comparison showing that this specified new domain has a minimum.
module.boundary: 0 is the infimum of Q+ but is not in Q+, so it is not the smallest positive rational. Repeated halving also does not mean reaching 0 in finitely many steps. Sets with fixed denominators, finite precision, or other discrete domains can have a smallest element. A contradiction must arise from the target assumption and consistent premises, not from algebraic error, circular reasoning, or switching domains.
module.reflection: Someone also halves 1/100 in T={n/100 : n is a positive integer}, obtaining the smaller 1/200. Why does this fail to refute T’s minimum? Compared with the r/2 argument in Q+, identify the domain-membership check that fails.

references.citation: Richard Hammack. Book of Proof, 3rd edition (edition 3.4), 6.1 Proving Statements with Contradiction. Richard Hammack (2018; revised 2025).
references.use: Supports the proof structure of assuming the negation of the target statement, deriving a conflict with that assumption through valid reasoning, and then rejecting the assumption; this example is not presented as a historical-discovery narrative.

references.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, 1.8 Proof by Contradiction. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
references.use: Supports the logical structure of contradiction and the need to check validity of the reasoning; the positive-rational minimum example here is independently derived from the definition and ordering of rational numbers rather than attributed as a historical example from the textbook.

articles.summaryZh: 许澄要给自动连点功能写一条对任意规模成立的规则保证。截图只能检验有限规模的实现；她把抽象规则单独拿出来，从n=1起证明任意k的正确结构都能在不改删旧点线的情况下推进到k+1。
storyParagraphsZh: 许澄要给自动连点功能写规格：从1个点开始，每次只加入一个全新点，并只新增1条边把新点接到已有连通结构；已有点和边都不改不删，也不允许成环。她画到5个点，边数是0、1、2、3、4。产品经理问：“一百个点呢？”五张截图答不了这个问题。
她又让测试环境生成20个点，得到19条边，但马上把这张图也归到测试附件。更多样例只能说明这些规模没有暴露实现问题；规格真正要保证的是：如果程序始终遵守刚才那条抽象生长规则，那么对任意正整数n，结构都有n−1条边。她把这句话单独写到规格页上，和“当前测试通过”分开。
许澄在规格页左边写下P(n)：按这条规则得到n个点时，有n−1条边，n是大于等于1的整数。右边还摆着五张截图。她先画一颗孤零零的点，旁边填0=1−1，在左栏第一格写“P(1)成立”。下一格的k先留空；它要接住的不能只是第五张图，还得是任何一个已经按规则长出的结构。
接着她取任意k≥1，只暂时假设P(k)：k个点时有k−1条边。下一步加入的是一个此前不存在的新点，只新增一条连接到旧结构的边，其他点和边保持不动，因此边数变成(k−1)+1=k，而k=(k+1)−1。这个推导没有用到k是5、20还是500。
评审时，工程师问：“如果代码偶尔把新点连出两条边呢？”许澄把左栏的P(1)和任意k→k+1递过去：它们保证按规则长出的结构都有正确边数。右栏的1、5、20点回归测试也递过去：这些还要检查程序有没有真的遵守每步一点一边的限制。工程师的问题没有被左栏消掉，它仍在右栏等待实现检查。
提交时，她把五点图和20点图装进测试附件，规格正文保留基础情形和任意k的推导。页脚的两个方框没有一起勾上：“规则结论已证明”旁边有一个勾，“软件实现已验证”旁边还是空的。那张第五个点的截图也夹在后面，连线画得很齐。
articles.overallZh: 数学归纳法通过基础情形和对任意k的归纳步，把自然数命题推广到全部合法n。本篇证明的是明确抽象生长规则下的边数结论；有限测试不能替代证明，证明也不能保证软件实现规则无误。
explanationParagraphsZh: 基础情形n=1给0=n−1。若任意k≥1时有k−1条边，加入全新点并只加1条连接旧结构的边，且不改删其他点线，就得到k=(k+1)−1。
归纳假设只是假设P(k)，不是先假设所有n成立。截图检查实现；抽象证明只覆盖题目给定的生长规则。

moduleZh.intro: 把抽象规则正确与软件实现正确拆开：前者用基础情形和任意k推进证明，后者继续靠测试检查。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从一个点的起点到任意n的规则保证
diagramSteps: 固定n≥1及每步只添全新点和一条边的规则
验证P(1)：1点0边
对任意k≥1只假设P(k)
加入新点且不改删旧结构，推出P(k+1)
把全称证明与有限软件测试分栏保留
diagramStepNotes: 规则还要求新边接入已有连通结构且不成环。
基础情形0=1−1，不能省略。
归纳假设只针对当前任意k。
1、5、20点截图只能测试实现，不构成全称证明。
mapping: 五点与20点截图 → 有限软件测试样例。
P(1) → 全称证明的起点。
“全新点+一条新边”规则 → k到k+1的实际结构变化。
规格页左右两栏 → 数学保证与实现验收的边界。
moduleZh.boundary: 结论只适用于给定生长规则，不适用于任意图。不能跳过基础情形、不能假设所有n已成立，也不能在归纳步偷偷修改或删除旧点线。数学证明不验证具体代码是否正确实现这些规则。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果20个点的测试也通过，为什么仍需要任意k→k+1的推导？反过来，这个推导为什么也抓不到代码偶尔多加一条边的bug？

referencesZh.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, Chapter 5: Induction. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
referencesZh.use: 支持基础情形与对任意合法k的归纳步共同建立全称命题，并支持有限核验不能替代一般证明。

referencesZh.citation: Stanford University. CS103: Mathematical Induction, Part I, condensed lecture slides. Fall 2024, 23 October 2024.
referencesZh.use: 支持基础情形、归纳假设、归纳步和论域覆盖；该教学资料不作为这种证明方法的历史发明来源。

articles.title: The Fifth Screenshot
articles.summary: Xu Cheng needs to write a rule guarantee for an automatic point-connection feature that holds at any scale. Screenshots can test only finitely many sizes of the implementation; she separates out the abstract rule and proves from n=1 that any correct structure at an arbitrary k can advance to k+1 without changing or deleting existing points or edges.
storyParagraphs: Xu Cheng needs to write the specification for an automatic point-connection feature: start with one point; each step adds exactly one new point and exactly one new edge connecting that point to the existing connected structure; existing points and edges are neither changed nor deleted, and cycles are not allowed. She draws up to five points and gets 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 edges. The product manager asks, “What about one hundred points?” Five screenshots cannot answer that question.

She has the test environment generate 20 points and gets 19 edges, but immediately moves that image into the test appendix as well. More examples only show that those tested sizes have not exposed an implementation problem. What the specification really needs to guarantee is this: if the program always follows the abstract growth rule just stated, then for every positive integer n, the structure has n−1 edges. She writes that sentence separately on the specification page, apart from “current tests pass.”

On the left of the specification page, Xu Cheng writes P(n): a structure grown by this rule has n−1 edges when it has n points, where n is an integer at least 1. The five screenshots sit on the right. She draws a single point, writes 0=1−1 beside it, and fills the first left-hand box with “P(1) holds.” She leaves k blank in the next box: it must stand for any structure already grown by the rule, rather than only the fifth picture.

Next she takes an arbitrary k≥1 and assumes only P(k): with k points there are k−1 edges. The next step adds a point that did not previously exist and exactly one edge connecting it to the old structure, while all other points and edges remain unchanged. The edge count therefore becomes (k−1)+1=k, and k=(k+1)−1. The derivation does not depend on whether k is 5, 20, or 500.

During review, an engineer asks, “What if the code occasionally connects the new point with two edges?” Xu Cheng hands over the left column with P(1) and the arbitrary k→k+1 step: they guarantee the correct edge count for structures grown by the rule. She also hands over the right column with the 1-, 5-, and 20-point regression tests, which still need to check whether the program follows the one-point, one-edge limit. The left column does not dispose of the engineer’s question; it remains in the right column for implementation checks.

When she submits the specification, she places the five-point and 20-point images in the test appendix and keeps the base case and arbitrary-k derivation in the main text. The two boxes at the foot of the page are not checked together: “rule result proved” has a tick, while “software implementation verified” is still empty. The fifth-point screenshot sits behind the page, its lines neatly drawn.
articles.overall: Mathematical induction extends a statement over the natural numbers by combining a base case with an induction step for an arbitrary k. This article proves the edge-count result for a specific abstract growth rule; finite tests cannot replace that proof, and the proof does not guarantee that software implements the rule correctly.
explanationParagraphs: The base case n=1 gives 0=n−1. If an arbitrary k≥1 has k−1 edges, then adding one new point and exactly one edge to the old structure, without changing or deleting any existing points or edges, gives k=(k+1)−1.
The induction hypothesis assumes only P(k), not that all n are already true. Screenshots test the implementation; the abstract proof covers only the stated growth rule.

module.intro: Separate correctness of the abstract rule from correctness of the software implementation: prove the former with a base case and an arbitrary-k step, and keep testing the latter.
module.diagramTitle: From the One-Point Start to a Rule Guarantee for Any n
diagramSteps: Fix n≥1 and the rule that each step adds one new point and one edge
Verify P(1): one point and zero edges
For an arbitrary k≥1, assume only P(k)
Add the new point without changing or deleting the old structure and derive P(k+1)
Keep the universal proof and finite software tests in separate columns
diagramStepNotes: The rule also requires the new edge to connect into the existing connected structure without creating a cycle.
The base case is 0=1−1 and cannot be omitted.
The induction hypothesis applies only to the current arbitrary k.
The edge count becomes (k−1)+1=k=(k+1)−1.
Screenshots at 1, 5, and 20 points test the implementation; they do not constitute a universal proof.
mapping: Five-point and 20-point screenshots → finite software test cases.
P(1) → the starting point of the universal proof.
“One new point + one new edge” rule → the actual structural change from k to k+1.
Two columns on the specification page → the boundary between mathematical guarantee and implementation validation.
module.boundary: The conclusion applies only to the stated growth rule, not to arbitrary graphs. The base case cannot be skipped, one cannot assume that all n are already true, and the induction step cannot secretly alter or delete existing points or edges. The mathematical proof does not verify that a particular implementation follows the rules correctly.
module.reflection: If the 20-point test also passes, why is the arbitrary k→k+1 derivation still needed? Conversely, why can that derivation fail to catch a bug that occasionally adds an extra edge?

references.citation: Eric Lehman, F. Thomson Leighton, Albert R. Meyer. Mathematics for Computer Science, Chapter 5: Induction. MIT OpenCourseWare, revised 18 May 2015.
references.use: Supports establishing a universal statement through a base case plus an induction step for an arbitrary valid k, and supports the point that finite checking does not replace a general proof.

references.citation: Stanford University. CS103: Mathematical Induction, Part I, condensed lecture slides. Fall 2024, 23 October 2024.
references.use: Supports the base case, induction hypothesis, induction step, and domain coverage; this teaching material is not treated as the historical invention source of the proof method.

articles.summaryZh: 健身房经理用App问卷决定是否提前晚课，100名App会员全部回答且80%支持。她随后发现另100名前台/电话会员从未见到问卷，并通过补访得到其中20人支持；完整200人支持率因此是50%，原便利渠道系统性偏向了更支持调整的一组。
storyParagraphsZh: 健身房经理乔安想把晚间团课提前一小时，先在App里发了快捷问卷。100名经常用App预约的活跃会员都回答了，其中80人支持。她把“80%支持”写在便签上，已经准备通知教练下月改时间。
前台主管拿来完整活跃会员名单时，乔安才发现目标总体其实有200人：另外100人主要靠前台或电话预约，从未看到App入口。她这一周发过五轮提醒，系统显示500次弹窗，但那只是对同一批可见会员的重复触达，不是500名不同受访者。
乔安先停住改课通知，没有拿“B组也有100人”去猜他们会怎么答。为了弄清覆盖缺口，她让前台用同一句问题补访那100名从未入样的会员；前台逐人核对名字，100人全部回应，其中20人支持、80人不支持。B组的20%是补访得到的，不是从A组推出来的。
两组放在一起后，A组支持80/100，B组20/100，全体支持人数是100/200=50%。这并不意味着50%自动告诉她课表该怎么改；它真正推翻的是另一件事：只看App渠道的80%，不能代表原本定义的200名活跃会员。
乔安把教练通知暂时留在草稿箱，打开下一次调查的收件名单，把默认的App名单换成完整会员表。前台和电话预约者的名字也列在上面，旁边留出“已回应”“未回应”两栏。她在发送前还要核对选人办法；这次先把名单里看不见的一半找回来，通知的时间暂不填。
办公室门旁那张80%便签没有被扔掉。乔安把它翻到背面，补写“100名App会员”；旁边的新表格写着(80+20)/200=50%。五轮500次弹窗记录也还在，只是不再被当成500个独立人。教练的改课通知仍停在草稿箱，等乔安把调查对象和决策标准重新说清楚。
articles.overallZh: 抽样偏差是选择、覆盖或未回应机制与所测结果相关，使样本统计量系统性偏离目标总体的现象；不等于所有不等概率选择都有偏差。本篇的App渠道完全漏掉偏好不同的B组，因此80%不能代表全部200人。
explanationParagraphsZh: 抽样偏差来自入样机会与结果相关造成的系统偏离。补访后A=80/100、B=20/100，全体100/200=50%，说明App便利样本只准确描述A组。
500次弹窗只是重复邀请，不是500个独立会员。若B完全缺失且偏好未知，仅知道B有100人也不能靠权重恢复其均值；不等概率本身并不必然有偏。

moduleZh.intro: 先让便利渠道给出可行动的80%，再通过完整名单和补访揭示谁从未有机会进入样本。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 100份完整App答卷怎样被另外100名未覆盖会员改写
diagramSteps: 定义目标总体为200名活跃会员
识别App只覆盖A组100人且80人支持
确认五轮500次只是重复邀请同一覆盖群体
补访此前未入样的B组100人并得到20人支持
合并为100/200=50%并暂停外推80%的决定
diagramStepNotes: 目标总体先于便利渠道定义。
A组100%回应并不能补进B组。
重复触达次数不能当独立样本人数。
B组20%来自本故事的完整补访设定，不由A推算。
50%描述完整虚构总体，但不唯一决定课表行动。
mapping: 80%便签 → 对A组准确却被错误外推的结果。
完整会员名单 → 暴露100名未覆盖成员。
前台补访表 → 让B组结果真正进入数据。
翻到背面的便签 → 角色行为从立即改课转为先修正调查依据。
moduleZh.boundary: 这是虚构有限总体和完全补访，用来展示覆盖机制。现实调查还会有抽样误差、未回应和测量误差。若某组完全未入样且结果未知，仅知道组规模不能恢复其均值；权重需要已知选择机制或其他可辩护信息。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果补访B组时仍有20人没有回应，你还有什么依据把50%写成全体会员的答案？

referencesZh.citation: Statistics Canada. Statistics: Power from Data!, §3.2.3 Non-probability sampling.
referencesZh.use: 支持非概率选取、自选和覆盖问题，以及大样本不能自动消除系统偏离。

referencesZh.citation: Statistics Canada. Questions to ask about surveys.
referencesZh.use: 支持明确目标总体、抽样框、概率选取与未回应风险；入样概率不必相等，但必须被设计和理解。

articles.title: The 80% Note Gets Turned Over
articles.summary: A gym manager uses an app survey to decide whether to move an evening class earlier. All 100 app members respond and 80% support the change. She then discovers another 100 front-desk/phone members who never saw the survey and follows up with them, finding 20 supporters. The full 200-member support rate is therefore 50%, showing that the convenience channel systematically overrepresented the more supportive group.
storyParagraphs: Gym manager Qiao An wants to move an evening group class one hour earlier, so she starts with a quick survey in the app. All 100 active members who regularly book through the app respond, and 80 support the change. She writes “80% support” on a sticky note and is already preparing to notify the instructor about next month’s schedule.

When the front-desk supervisor brings the complete active-member list, Qiao An realizes that the target population actually contains 200 people. Another 100 mainly book at the front desk or by phone and never saw the app entry point. During the week she sent five rounds of reminders and the system shows 500 pop-up displays, but those are repeated contacts with the same visible group, not 500 different respondents.

Qiao An pauses the schedule-change notice and does not use “group B also has 100 people” to guess how they would answer. To investigate the coverage gap, she asks the front desk to follow up with those 100 members who were never sampled, using the same question. The front desk checks the names one by one. All 100 respond: 20 support the change and 80 do not. Group B’s 20% comes from the follow-up, not from extrapolating group A.

Putting the two groups together, group A has 80/100 supporters and group B 20/100, for 100/200=50% support overall. That does not mean 50% automatically tells her how the class schedule should be changed. What it overturns is a different claim: the 80% from the app channel cannot represent the originally defined population of 200 active members.

Qiao An leaves the instructor notice in drafts and opens the recipient list for the next survey, replacing the default app list with the complete membership table. Front-desk and phone bookers are listed too, beside columns for “responded” and “not responded.” She still needs to check how people will be selected before sending. For now, she restores the half previously absent from the list and leaves the notification time blank.

The 80% sticky note beside the office door is not thrown away. Qiao An flips it over and adds “100 app members.” Beside it, a new sheet reads (80+20)/200=50%. The records of five rounds and 500 pop-up displays remain as well, but no one treats them as 500 independent people. The instructor notification is still in drafts while Qiao An clarifies the survey population and the decision criteria.
articles.overall: Sampling bias occurs when selection, coverage, or nonresponse mechanisms are related to the outcome being measured, causing sample statistics to differ systematically from the target population. It does not mean that every unequal-probability selection is biased. Here, the app channel completely misses group B, whose preferences differ, so 80% cannot represent all 200 members.
explanationParagraphs: Sampling bias is systematic deviation caused by the relationship between inclusion opportunity and the outcome. After follow-up, A=80/100 and B=20/100, giving 100/200=50% overall, showing that the app convenience sample accurately described only group A.

The 500 pop-ups are repeated invitations, not 500 independent members. If group B is completely missing and its preferences are unknown, knowing only that it contains 100 people is insufficient to recover its mean through weighting; unequal probabilities alone do not necessarily imply bias.

module.intro: Let a convenient channel first produce an actionable 80%, then use the complete list and follow-up to reveal who never had a chance to enter the sample.
module.diagramTitle: How 100 Complete App Responses Are Rewritten by 100 Previously Uncovered Members
diagramSteps: Define the target population as 200 active members
Identify that the app covers only group A of 100, with 80 supporters
Recognize that five rounds and 500 displays are repeated invitations to the same covered group
Follow up with the previously uncovered 100 members in group B and obtain 20 supporters
Combine to 100/200=50% and pause the decision that extrapolated 80%
diagramStepNotes: The target population is defined before choosing the convenience channel.
A 100% response rate in group A does not bring group B into the sample.
Repeated contact counts are not independent sample sizes.
Group B’s 20% comes from the complete follow-up in this story, not from inference from A.
50% describes the complete fictional population but does not uniquely determine the schedule decision.
mapping: 80% sticky note → a result accurate for group A but incorrectly extrapolated.
Complete member list → reveals 100 uncovered members.
Front-desk follow-up sheet → actually brings group B’s outcomes into the data.
Flipped sticky note → the character changes behavior from immediate schedule change to repairing the survey basis first.
module.boundary: This is a fictional finite population with complete follow-up, used to illustrate a coverage mechanism. Real surveys also involve sampling error, nonresponse, and measurement error. If a group is entirely unsampled and its outcomes are unknown, its mean cannot be recovered from group size alone; weighting requires a known selection mechanism or other defensible information.
module.reflection: If 20 members of group B still did not respond to the follow-up, what evidence would you need before writing 50% as the result for all members?

references.citation: Statistics Canada. Statistics: Power from Data!, §3.2.3 Non-probability sampling.
references.use: Supports non-probability selection, self-selection, and coverage problems, as well as the point that a large sample does not automatically remove systematic deviation.

references.citation: Statistics Canada. Questions to ask about surveys.
references.use: Supports defining the target population and sampling frame, using probability selection, and considering nonresponse risk; inclusion probabilities need not be equal, but they must be designed and understood.

articles.title: The Reward That Ruined the Best Bread
articles.summary: Whenever a baker rewards the day's best loaf, the next one is worse, so he concludes that praise destroys skill.
articles.summaryZh: 师傅每次奖励最好的面包，第二天它总会变差，于是他认定赞美会毁掉手艺。
storyParagraphs: Master baker Orun wanted the royal bread contract and began ranking every oven load. The day's highest loaf received a red sugar flower; the lowest baker was scolded before the whole shop. Winners often scored worse the next morning, while last-place bakers usually improved. Orun saw a clean lesson: praise softened workers and humiliation sharpened them. He intensified the rule, certain that the next month's rising average would prove his management.

One wet Tuesday, baker Mina scored 54 against her usual range near 76 to 84. A leaking oven door and damp flour had joined her own mistake. Orun dismissed her on the spot. The next day, without any scolding, a reserve baker using the repaired oven scored 79. In the same week Jaro's exceptional 97 followed perfect heat and unusually dry flour; after receiving the red flower he scored 83. Orun called both movements evidence for punishment, although each result had been selected because it was extreme.

Bookkeeper Sali plotted ten prior batches for every baker. Repeated scores shared skill but also varied with moisture, temperature, tasting error, and chance. A person observed at an unusually high or low combination was unlikely to receive the same combination next time. Among twelve unpunished low scores from earlier records, the next batch rose by an average of eleven points. Among ten unrewarded high scores, the next fell by nine. Movement toward ordinary ranges appeared without Orun's words.

Orun snapped the chalk and said Sali had made all feedback meaningless. She opened two blank ledger pages. On one she wrote 'chosen because yesterday was extreme'; on the other, 'changed routine versus unchanged routine.' Then she ruled spaces for several baseline batches, matched ovens, and blind tasting. The first page already predicted some rebound before anyone spoke. Only the second could help separate a new practice from that background movement. Orun stared at Mina's dismissal mark and signed the trial order with the broken chalk still beside his hand.

The guild hearing was two days away. Orun stared at Mina's dismissal mark until the broken chalk stained his thumb, then admitted that his strongest example did not isolate the effect of shouting. He rehired her with back pay, forfeited his personal contract bonus, and replaced public rankings with a trial. Half the ovens received a new temperature checklist, half continued the old routine for a month, and evaluators tasted loaves without knowing which group made them. Immediate safety errors were still corrected; spectacle no longer stood in for evidence.

A month later the checklist group improved beyond its prior range and comparison group, though the shop kept watching. On the next judging day Mina baked a 96. Orun placed the red flower beside the loaf, then wrote her previous ten scores underneath instead of predicting tomorrow. The flower's sugar edge softened in the steam, while the row of numbers remained visible on the slate.
storyParagraphsZh: 面包师奥伦想拿下王室供货合同，开始给每炉打分。当天最高分可得一朵红糖花，最低分的人要当众挨骂。奇怪的是，冠军次日常变差，末名却往往回升。奥伦认定赞美使人松懈，羞辱才能磨快手艺，于是把奖罚加重，等着下月均分证明自己的管理。
一个潮湿星期二，米娜只得五十四分，她平日多在七十六至八十四之间。漏风炉门、受潮面粉和她自己的失误碰到一起，奥伦仍当场辞退她。次日，备用师傅使用修好的炉子得七十九分。同周，雅罗遇到恰好炉温与干燥面粉，烤出九十七分，领红花后第二天得八十三。奥伦把两次变化都算成责骂有效，尽管他们正因成绩极端才被挑出来。
账房萨莉画出每名师傅此前十炉。重复成绩既含手艺，也受湿度、温度、品评分歧和偶然波动影响；某次碰上异常好坏组合，下次很难原样重现。旧账里，十二次没有受罚的低分之后，下一炉平均上升十一分；十次没有受奖的高分之后，下一炉平均下降九分。没有奥伦的话，成绩照样向个人常态靠近。
奥伦折断粉笔，说萨莉把所有反馈都说成了无用。她摊开两张空白账页，一张写“因昨日极端而入选”，另一张写“改变流程与保持原样相比较”，随后画出多次基线、相似炉位和盲评栏。第一张纸在任何人开口前就会出现部分回摆；第二张才可能把新做法从这种背景变化里分开。奥伦盯着米娜名字后的解雇记号，断粉笔仍搁在手边，最后在试验单上签字。
工会听证只剩两天。奥伦盯着米娜名字后的解雇记号，直到断粉笔把拇指染白，才承认最有力的例子没有隔离吼叫的作用。他补发工资请回米娜，放弃个人合同奖金，改做一个月试验：一半炉位使用新温度清单，另一半保持旧流程，品评人不知道面包来自哪组。安全错误仍即时纠正，公开羞辱不再冒充证据。
一个月后，清单组的改善超过自身旧范围和对照组，面包坊仍继续观察。下一次评比，米娜烤出九十六分。奥伦把红糖花放在面包旁，又在下面写出她过去十炉，而没有预言明天。蒸汽让糖花边缘微微发软，石板上的那排数字仍清楚。
explanationParagraphs: Regression to the mean occurs when cases are selected for an extreme observation and repeated measurements are imperfectly correlated and contain random variation; later values tend on average to be less extreme. It is a conditional statistical pattern, not a causal force, and does not prove an intervention ineffective. Controls, repeated baselines, and reliable measurement help distinguish it.
explanationParagraphsZh: 均值回归发生在按极端观测选择对象，而重复测量相关性不完美且含随机变化时，后续结果平均会较不极端。它是条件统计模式，不是把对象拉回的因果力量，也不证明干预无效。对照、多次基线和可靠测量有助于区分，也要避免只挑极端值做前后比较。

articles.summaryZh: 无编号模块只可能来自A或B两批；对眼前同型号返修件，当天记录给A/B先验1/4与3/4。蓝贴在A/B中的条件概率为1/2与1/6，更新后两边各1/2，于是林珂改变查找策略，但并未确认来源。
storyParagraphsZh: 维修台上有一只掉了编号的同型号充电模块，林珂得在A、B两本厚检修记录里找它。任务记录明确这类当天返修件只来自A、B两批；其中A约占1/4，B约占3/4。这些比例只是眼前这批同型号返修件的估计。两本记录各有几十页，她原本把B本先抽出来，准备优先查B。
翻模块时，她看见背面还粘着一角蓝色质检贴。当天批次记录另给出：若来自A，出现这种蓝贴的概率估为1/2；若来自B，约为1/6。蓝贴在A中更常见，但林珂没有把这个1/2直接当成“来源A的概率”，她把它记在便签上，给另一个来源也留了位置。
她把来源写成互斥且穷尽的H_A、H_B，把蓝贴记为E。A的未归一化权重是1/4×1/2=1/8；B的是3/4×1/6=1/8。总权重1/4，所以P(H_A|E)=1/2，P(H_B|E)=1/2。这里P(E|H_A)和P(H_A|E)数值碰巧都为1/2，却是不同条件量。
林珂把A记录本也抽到桌上。原来“先翻B，没找到再查A”的计划停了下来。两本索引都能先按日期查接口批次码，她把当天那一栏各夹一张纸，准备从这里往下找。A原本只有四分之一的把握，现在已经和B一样；几十页的B记录不再独占她的第一轮查找。便签上的数字还不足以填来源栏，却足以让A本从书架挪到手边。
接口码还没查到，蓝贴已经用过一次。林珂把它的两项权重留在便签上，没有又乘一遍；那不会给来源增加一条新线索。她准备接着查两批的接口码记录，但便签暂时只算到各1/2。若下一条信息和蓝贴有关，它就得连同已知蓝贴一起处理，而不能再被当成一枚无关的贴纸。
模块放在两本记录之间，背面的蓝贴还剩一角。便签上的两个1/8各引出一个1/2，A、B的索引页各夹着一张纸。她先沿当天的接口码栏找下去，两本书都没有收回。维修单上的来源栏依然空着。
articles.overallZh: 贝叶斯更新在互斥且穷尽的假设下，用先验概率乘各假设下当前证据的条件概率，再归一化得到后验。本篇后验从1/4对3/4变为1/2对1/2，足以改变人物的查找计划，但不等于来源已确认。
explanationParagraphsZh: A权重1/4×1/2=1/8，B权重3/4×1/6=1/8；总权重1/4，因此后验各为1/2。P(E|H_A)与P(H_A|E)在本题数值恰相同，但定义不同。
后续证据可以与蓝贴相关，更新时须使用正确的条件关系；后验概率本身也不唯一决定最优查找动作。

moduleZh.intro: 让先验先影响原查找顺序，再用蓝贴重新分配来源权重，并把概率更新与行动选择分开。
diagramSteps: 限定A/B为眼前同型返修件的互斥穷尽来源
算两个未归一化权重都为1/8
用总权重1/4归一化得到各1/2
改变查找策略但不把后验当来源确认或唯一决策
diagramStepNotes: 先验只适用于本题当天同型号返修件。
A和B权重恰好相同。
后续相关证据需按条件关系建模，不能机械重复乘同一证据。
mapping: 最先抽出的B记录本 → 先验影响的初始行动。
蓝贴 → 当前证据E。
两个1/8便签 → 更新前的未归一化权重。
并排的A/B索引页 → 后验改变计划但未确认来源。
moduleZh.boundary: A/B互斥穷尽和数值均为本题给定估计，不是普遍频率。P(E|H)与P(H|E)不能混淆，即便本题某两个数值碰巧相同。后续证据无需普遍独立，但必须正确建模条件关系；概率更新也不自动给出唯一最优行动。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么蓝贴足以让林珂放弃“先只查B”，却还不足以让她把来源栏填成A？

referencesZh.citation: Thomas Bayes. An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London 53 (1763), 370–418; communicated by Richard Price.
referencesZh.use: 作为逆概率与条件概率推理的历史来源；不把现代符号、维修场景或本篇虚构数值归给原作者。

articles.title: Two Logs Beside a Blue Sticker
articles.summary: An unnumbered module can come only from batches A or B. For the same-model returns in question, the day’s records assign priors of 1/4 and 3/4. The blue sticker has conditional probabilities 1/2 and 1/6 under A and B, so the updated probabilities become 1/2 each. Lin Ke changes her search strategy without confirming the source.
storyParagraphs: An unnumbered charging module sits on the repair bench, and Lin Ke needs to locate it in two thick service logs for batches A and B. The task record states that same-model returns that day come only from those two batches: about 1/4 from A and 3/4 from B. Those proportions are estimates only for the same-model returns in this task. Each log has dozens of pages, so she initially pulls out the B log and plans to search B first.

When she turns the module over, she notices the corner of a blue quality-control sticker still attached to the back. The day’s batch record also states that if a module comes from A, the estimated probability of this blue sticker is 1/2; if it comes from B, the estimate is about 1/6. The sticker is more common under A, but Lin Ke does not treat that 1/2 directly as “the probability that the source is A.” She writes it on a note and leaves space for the other source.

She writes the mutually exclusive and exhaustive sources as H_A and H_B and labels the sticker evidence E. A’s unnormalized weight is 1/4×1/2=1/8. B’s is 3/4×1/6=1/8. The total weight is 1/4, so P(H_A|E)=1/2 and P(H_B|E)=1/2. In this problem, P(E|H_A) and P(H_A|E) happen to have the same numerical value, 1/2, but they are different conditional quantities.

Lin Ke pulls the A log onto the desk too. She pauses her original plan of searching B first and A only if needed. Both indexes let her look up interface batch codes by date, so she clips the relevant column in each and starts there. A had only a one-in-four chance; now it stands level with B. The dozens of pages in the B log no longer occupy her entire first search. The numbers on the note cannot fill the source field, but they are enough to bring the A book down from the shelf.

The interface code has not been checked yet; the blue sticker has already been used once. Lin Ke leaves its two weights on the note rather than multiplying them again, which would add no new clue about the source. She prepares to check the code records for both batches, but for now the note ends at 1/2 each. If the next information is related to the sticker, it must be handled together with what is already known about the sticker, rather than treated as unrelated evidence.

The module sits between the two logs, a corner of the blue sticker still on its back. Each 1/8 on the note leads to a 1/2, and one slip marks the index in each book. She starts down the interface-code column for the date, keeping both books open. The source field on the repair form remains blank.
articles.overall: Bayesian updating combines prior probabilities with the conditional probability of the observed evidence under each mutually exclusive and exhaustive hypothesis, then normalizes to obtain posterior probabilities. Here the posterior moves from 1/4 versus 3/4 to 1/2 versus 1/2, enough to change the character’s search plan without confirming the source.
explanationParagraphs: A’s weight is 1/4×1/2=1/8 and B’s is 3/4×1/6=1/8. The total weight is 1/4, so both posteriors are 1/2. P(E|H_A) and P(H_A|E) happen to be numerically equal here, but they have different definitions.
Later evidence may be related to the blue sticker; any further update must use the correct conditional relationship. Posterior probabilities also do not uniquely determine the best search action.

module.intro: Let the prior affect the original search order, then use the blue-sticker evidence to redistribute source weights while keeping probability updating separate from action choice.
module.diagramTitle: How A/B Moves from 1/4 vs 3/4 to 1/2 vs 1/2
diagramSteps: Restrict A/B to the mutually exclusive and exhaustive sources for these same-model returns
Write priors 1/4 and 3/4 and blue-sticker likelihoods 1/2 and 1/6
Compute both unnormalized weights as 1/8
Normalize by total weight 1/4 to obtain 1/2 each
Change the search strategy without treating the posterior as source confirmation or a unique decision rule
diagramStepNotes: The priors apply only to the same-model returns in this task and on that day.
The A and B weights are exactly equal.
Later related evidence must be modeled through the correct conditional relationship; the same evidence is not mechanically multiplied again.
mapping: B log pulled first → the action initially influenced by the prior.
Blue sticker → the current evidence E.
Two 1/8 notes → the unnormalized weights after incorporating the evidence.
A/B index pages side by side → the posterior changes the plan without confirming the source.
module.boundary: A/B being mutually exclusive and exhaustive, and all numerical values, are assumptions for this task rather than universal frequencies. P(E|H) and P(H|E) must not be confused even when two numerical values happen to match here. Later evidence need not generally be independent, but its conditional relationship must be modeled correctly; probability updating also does not automatically specify a unique optimal action.
module.reflection: Why is the blue sticker enough for Lin Ke to abandon “search only B first,” but still not enough for her to fill the source field with A?
